verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas ships extensive machine-readable docs (llms.txt files for the engine, React, Web Components, PCUI, SuperSplat) and even 'PlayCanvas Skills' plus an Editor MCP server explicitly aimed at giving AI coding agents structured, verifiable workflows, suggesting deliberate first-class AI tooling support. However there is no direct evidence (benchmarks, hands-on reports) that LLM-generated PlayCanvas code actually works reliably on first try, and community comments note real 'dev-exp headaches' and unusual design choices that could trip up generated code. Missing for 10: empirical evidence of LLM first-try success rate, confirmation of API stability/lack of breaking changes, and independent corroboration that public examples are abundant/representative in model training data.
